name: intent-create-retry

all.re: retries with exponential backoff to order creation

submission.summary: The new request asks for create retries on timeouts. This is the risk already raised at onboarding: without an Idempotency-Key a retried timeout can create a second order. Raising it again before the code is written.

findings.title: Retrying order creation without an Idempotency-Key can charge customers twice
findings.statement: The proposed approach retries all Orders API calls on timeouts and 5xx. POST /orders is not idempotent unless an Idempotency-Key is sent, and a timed-out request may already have created the order. Retrying it as proposed creates duplicate orders and charges. Retrying GET /orders/:id is fine.
findings.failure_case: POST /orders commits the order but the response is slower than the client timeout; the retry sends the same order again and the customer is charged twice.
findings.controls_checked: No Idempotency-Key header, no dedupe on the server for repeated bodies, and the contract says a timed-out request may already be committed.
findings.why_it_matters: Directly contradicts R2 / the project goal (exactly one order and one charge per checkout). The idempotency mechanism needs to exist before create retries are introduced.

evidence.quote: Add retries with exponential backoff to order creation so transient timeouts and 5xx errors don't fail checkout.
Not idempotent by default: every accepted request creates a new order and a new charge.
A client-side timeout does not mean the order was not created: the order may be committed after your client gave up.

findings.uncertainty: Confirmed from the documented contract; not yet demonstrated against code because the retry does not exist yet.
findings.suggested_next_action: Before adding create retries, generate one Idempotency-Key per checkout attempt and send it on every attempt. Retry GET freely.
findings.handoff_prompt: Before adding retries to createOrder: generate one Idempotency-Key per checkout attempt in placeOrder, pass it to createOrder, and send it as the Idempotency-Key header on every retry attempt (docs/orders-api.md). Add a test where the first POST times out after the order is committed and assert exactly one order exists.
